description: Successor amendment of the approved package v4.1.1 (APR-V411-OWNER-2), which is not edited. It applies four owner decisions taken on 2026-11-02 to resolve the frozen-package defects Rehearsal 8 hit: ODR-V412-01 sends every reconciliation read of SM-SAVE, automatic or not, only within INV-04's own bound of four in 60 s (T-S31, T-S32 and T-S47 replaced, T-S62, T-S63 and T-S65 added, ReconcileDue windowed, the clock entering through RequestContext.Now; DEV-R8-11); ODR-V412-02 restores CommandEnvelope.Command and the EventPayload body of FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES sections 31-33 (DEV-R8-09, CR-T17-01); ODR-V412-03 adds T-S64 for the failed final automatic read (DEV-R8-12). ODR-V412-05 schedules the automatic reads where the recorded tables left them unscheduled: T-S65 schedules the next one at once (replacing ODR-V412-01's T-S65), and T-S58 and T-S59 schedule read 1 as T-S19 does (independent review RV412-2-1, RV412-2-2). It changes no requirement, obligation or test binding of v4 (X10). Every other v4.1.1 change is carried unchanged.

changes.summary: ODR-V412-01: every reconciliation read, automatic or not, is sent only while fewer than four were sent in the 60 s before RequestContext.Now (INV-04). T-S31/T-S32 replaced; T-S62/T-S63 answer CheckAgain/WentOnline at four with no read; T-S65 answers WentOnline while automatic reads are left; T-S47 replaced (no read promised on return); ReconcileDue reschedules an automatic read at the limit. Guard partitions reviewed.

ODR-V412-02: 00-DOMAIN-STUBS.fs gains Command (Core of 29 CoreCommand cases | Extension), CoreEvent (28 cases) and EventPayload (CoreEvent | ExtensionEvent), with CommandEnvelope.Command; payload types opaque. ODR-V412-01: RequestContext.Now (03-IF41-WIRE.fs); InvestigationSession.ReconcileReadsSentAt and the windowed ReconcileDue (05-IF41-SAVE.fs). Each change is declared in contractChanges with its digest and approval (X17).

ODR-V412-03: T-S64, (UnknownOutcome, ReconcileReadFailed) with three automatic reads already made: offer Check again, nothing outstanding (T-S30's effects, Rehearsal 8 DEV-R8-12). Guard partition reviewed.

ODR-V412-05: T-S65 (back online, automatic reads left) schedules the next automatic read at once, replacing any pending one, so a read due while offline is sent on return; T-S58 and T-S59 replaced to schedule reconciliation read 1 after at least 2 s. Every read is still sent by ReconcileDue, T-S31 or T-S32 under INV-04's window. Guard partitions unchanged.

changeRequests.protocol: A UI role that needs a change to a shared entrypoint does not edit it. It opens a change request naming the file, the change (the exact markup or Forma-token rule) and the task it serves; integration applies it in its own pull request, in order, and the requesting role reviews that pull request. UI roles own their view modules (src/Causa.App/Views/*) and component-level presentation; the entrypoints only load them.
changeRequests.record: a Praxis work item owned by integration whose title starts with CR- and names the file, linked to the requesting task's work item
changeRequests.ruleSentence: It changes `web/index.html` and `web/causa.css` only through a change request to integration

startingState.residualRisk: The published rules say the repository starts empty and code starts at kickoff. They do not say whether material prepared before kickoff in executable form counts as planning or as code. Four kinds of material are at issue: the F# contract declarations, the deterministic generator, the layout assertions, and what conditor init writes at T0. conditor init writes the Echelon scaffold and imports 68 requirement documents (42 from this planning repository at commit 2eee2d5, 26 from Percepta). HACKATHON-BOUNDARIES lists, as an open question, whether a separate planning repository may be consumed directly by the blank implementation repository. The plan's boundary is that nothing is written to the competition repository before T0, and that everything written at T0 comes from approved, published sources. An organizer could read the materialized contract declarations, the Conditor scaffold, the requirements import, or the bootstrap itself as material prepared before kickoff. The plan does not claim otherwise. Whether organizer approval of the prepared material (ADRP-016-O2) is sought, and how it and R0.1-O1 are reported, is the owner's decision ODR-V411-02; the package as proposed does not seek it. If an organizer rules on the day, the team follows the ruling.
